text: The MAPK cascade (growth factor -> receptor -> RAS -> RAF -> MEK -> ERK) is described as providing strong signal amplification. What is the mechanistic basis for this amplification?
choices: Each activated kinase can phosphorylate and activate many downstream kinase molecules, so the number of active molecules multiplies at each tier of the cascade
Each ligand-receptor binding event triggers clathrin-mediated endocytosis, which concentrates signaling molecules inside endosomes
Zero-order ultrasensitivity in the receptor-ligand binding step raises the effective Hill coefficient to between 20 and 40
Scaffold proteins such as KSR sequester all cascade components into a single static complex that blocks any downstream activation
explanation: Amplification in a kinase cascade arises because each activated kinase molecule can phosphorylate many substrate molecules, so the number of activated molecules grows at each successive tier. Receptor endocytosis (choice 1) is a trafficking mechanism related to signal termination and spatial control, not amplification. Zero-order ultrasensitivity (choice 2) is real in phosphorylation cycles but produces switch-like sensitivity rather than multi-tier amplification, and it is not a property of the receptor-ligand binding step. Scaffold proteins (choice 3) organize pathway components to preserve specificity; they do not block activation.
